IS : 10878 ( Part 2 ) -1984 



Indhn Standard 

FLAT-FORM SPRINGS 



( Reaffirmed 2006 ) 



PART 2 SPECIFICATION FOR SPRINGS MADE 
FROM RECTANGULAR COLD-ROLLED STRIPS 



1. Scope — Covers dimensions and quality specifications of cold formed flat springs made from 
rectangular cold-rolled strips up to 3*0 mm thick. 

1 .1 it does not cover the specification for disc springs and similar products. 

2. Drawing Specifications— The drawing should contain the following information : 

a) View of the flat form spring in unloaded condition. 

b) Dimensioned view of the spring in fitted condition. 

c) Material specification giving designation of grade of steel as indicated in 18:2507-1975 or 
other grade of steel or non-ferrous materia! alongwith : 

1) Hardness 

2) Surface treatment 

3) Edge condition like cut edges, natural edges and rounded edges. 

d) Additional information as for as possible like details of the function or application^ deflection 
of spring, loads, points of application of loads, type of loading, point of support, approximate 
developed dimension, maximum working temperature, etc. 

3. Modulus of elasticity of strips for design of fiat formad springs is as given below: 



Material 

1 ) Cold-rolled steel strip for springs as per IS : 2507-1 975 
'Cold-rolled steel strip for springs ( first revision Y 

2) Austentic stainless steel strips as per IS : 6911-1972 
'Stainless steel plate sheet and strip' 

3) Phosphor bronze strips as per IS : 7814-1975 'Phosphor 
bronze sheet strip and foil' 

4) Copper beryllium strips 



Modulus of Elasticity 
206 000 N/mm' 

190 200 N/mm^ 

105 000 Hlxx\m' 

127 000 N/mm^ 



3.1 The modulus of elasticity values specified as SI No, 2, 3 and 4 above are for genera! guidance 
only. Reference may be made to the material manufacturer for more exact values.

IS : 10878 ( Part 2 ) - 1984 

4.2 Requirements other than those specified in 4.1, shall be according to agreement between the 
purchaser and the supplier. 

5. Harxiness — As applicable for various material specified under 3. 

6. Surface Finish — To protect against corrosion, springs may be smeased with grease or oil. Other 
anticorrosive treatment may be applied subject to agreement between the purchaser and the 
manufacturer. 

7. Testing— Most flat formed springs require special load testing fixtures. While the points of 
anchoring and loading should be specified in the drawing, the fixture to be adopted for testing should 
be agreed upon between the purchaser and supplier. 

7.1 Endurance Testing — If required, the number of cycles, stroke frequency and the type of fixture 
should be agreed upon between the purchaser and the supplier. 

7.2 Adjustments for Manufacturing — When a load is specified at the fitted condition of a fiat spring, 
the unloaded height of the spring should be left to manufacturer's discretion for load adjustment.
